_comment: The launcher's pages, where a fresh install puts the apps it ships with, and how an app
with no place of its own finds one.
LunaCE's launcher has four built-in pages (apps, downloads, favorites, prefs) and reads
/etc/palm/launcher3/app-keywords-to-designator-map.txt for their display names and for a
keyword-to-page map; AppMonitor::pageDesignatorForWebOSApp tries an app's category first,
then each of its keywords. The reference TouchPad's own map renames favorites to GAMES and
prefs to SETTINGS, and maps webOS Archive's wosa-settings keyword to prefs.
'layout' is Lunacy's /etc/palm/default-launcher-page-layout.json, in the same shape as the
device's: the page each bundled app starts on, in the order it appears there. The device's
own file puts every settings app on prefs (Exhibition included, which carries no keywords),
the app catalogue alone on downloads, and names no favorites page at all - so Games starts
empty here too. Anything not named falls back to the keyword map, then to the first page.
Once the user moves an icon, their arrangement wins: this is only the starting point.
